claims.text: Applying a graphene-based solid-lubricant coating to a high-entropy alloy can reduce its coefficient of friction.
Applying a graphene-based solid-lubricant coating to a high-entropy alloy can reduce its wear rate.
The proposed intervention is application of a graphene-based solid-lubricant coating.
The coating should remain effective from -20°C to 200°C under dry sliding.
The coating should remain effective at normal loads up to 1000 N.
Graphene layers are the structural mediator produced by the coating intervention.
Easy shear between graphene layers reduces friction.
The graphene coating prevents direct metal-to-metal contact.
Preventing direct metal-to-metal contact reduces wear.
The graphene coating provides a barrier against oxidation and corrosion.
The coating will reduce coefficient of friction by at least 30% relative to the untreated alloy.
The coating will reduce wear rate by at least 50% relative to the untreated alloy.
Effectiveness is not claimed above 200°C, below -20°C, at loads exceeding 1000 N, or when other lubricants are present.
The magnitude of friction and wear reduction may depend on the high-entropy-alloy composition.
The magnitude of friction and wear reduction may depend on graphene-coating quality.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing coefficient of friction and wear rate for untreated and graphene-coated samples.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires at least 30% lower friction and 50% lower wear, but the falsification rule only requires the coated sample to be significantly lower than the control. Statistically significant improvements smaller than 30% and 50% would violate the quantitative prediction without falsifying the hypothesis under the stated rule.
